narrative.summary: The AI-driven Adaptive Traffic Control system demonstrated a decisive advantage over traditional fixed-time scheduling, achieving a 89.4% reduction in average waiting time and a 36.4% decrease in overall travel time.
keyObservations: Maximum intersection queue length peaked at 25 vehicles in Manual mode compared to 10 vehicles under Adaptive AI.
Vehicle throughput reached 1907 vehicles successfully cleared in Adaptive mode vs 1898 vehicles in Manual mode.
Mean vehicle speed across the network shifted by +34.1%, reflecting reduced start-stop friction at green transitions.
narrative.conclusion: By dynamically scaling green phase allocations based on live lane queue estimates and waiting time pressure rather than rigid clock intervals, the adaptive algorithm significantly mitigates congestion spikes while strictly honoring all pedestrian and clearance safety constraints.
